transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this wrap meeting started. As we all know, the set is scheduled for dismantling on Friday after the final stage shoot, and I need to approve the wrap disposition plan before we can lock it. The current draft sends scenic pieces to a general salvage vendor and places selected hero props in production storage. Before I can sign off, each department lead needs to confirm the exact disposition and environmental-compliance requirements for their area, and flag any exceptions to the draft plan with the exact corrective requirement so it goes on the record. Who wants to go first?

transcript.text: I need to flag an exception to the draft plan. The antique jukebox listed as a hero prop is actually a rented piece. I confirmed with the rental house yesterday that its agreement requires it to be returned to the owner in its original condition — it cannot go into production storage or salvage. The corrective requirement is to remove the jukebox from the hero props going to production storage and instead schedule its return to the rental house owner in original condition before Friday's dismantling.

transcript.text: I need to flag an exception to the draft plan on the environmental-compliance side. The production's city green-film incentive requires at least 85 percent of dismantled set material by weight to be diverted from landfill. I confirmed with the approved vendor this morning that their audited plan reaches that threshold only through separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record. However, the compliance packet still contains the general-salvage draft, which does not meet that requirement. The corrective requirement is to replace the general salvage vendor in the plan with the approved vendor's audited wood and metal recycling bin plan, and include the certified transfer record in the compliance packet before Mara can approve.
